doNotTarget: Practices owned by a larger group - the owner isn't the buyer

services.name: Tax Planning
services.line: A quarterly tax plan with a dollar figure on it: entity, comp, retirement, and depreciation moves flagged before their deadlines pass, not after filing.

services.name: Virtual CFO / FP&A
services.line: Monthly numbers you can run the practice on: clean books, one dashboard, and a monthly call that says what to do next and what it's worth.

guarantees: If the plan doesn't identify at least 2x its fee in annual tax savings, the plan is free. (Fee-back guarantee; promises nothing about the IRS.)
problemsSolved: Your accountant shows up in April to report what already happened, then goes quiet until extension season, so every tax-saving move expires unused.
proof: We handle multi-state, spiky-income returns for pro athletes and one of the largest law firms in Texas; your practice's return is not the hardest thing on our desk.
offer.guidingQuestion: What could you do for a prospect in 30 minutes that they'd happily pay $100 for?
offer.frontEndOffer: To be decided on this call. Whatever the answer to that question is, that's what goes in the first email.
leadMagnets: Option A - the value happens on the call. Your first 15 minutes IS the deliverable: you walk the owner through the handful of things you'd check on a business like theirs. It's your discovery call, renamed. Zero extra work. (If this one: what are the 6-8 things you'd actually check?)

Option B - we build them something before the call. We put together a short one-page brief per prospect from public information, so they get something real without you lifting a finger. (If this one: what would you want it to say?)

emails.subject: fyi {{first_name}}
emails.body: {{first_name}}, if we built you a one-page brief on what to look at before the Sept 15 estimate (we pull the filings and write it, no charge, you just reply "send"), worth a look?

emails.subject: {{city}} office
emails.body:
Dr. {{last_name}}, saw the {{city}} office was added last year. First-year entity and depreciation choices usually set a practice's tax bill for the next five. We run a 15-minute mid-year check on exactly this, no charge, you keep the checklist either way.

Worth doing?

items.ask: This is the objection we'll hear most. How do you answer it? Your words will be better than ours.
How do you want to be positioned - specialists in something, or generalists who do it all? Whatever's true.
What can we say in the copy, and which credentials would you like us to lead with?
Price range stated in the email, or held back for the call? Both work - stating it filters harder.

items.q: "Is a tax firm even allowed to email me like this?"
items.ask: You know these rules far better than we do. Anything we must say, or must never say, in an email going out under your name?

risks.prevention: Monitored daily, with warm-up buffers and rotation. Any dips reported to you the week it happens, with the fix attached.
First lists reviewed together before launch, and your feedback on every early positive tightens targeting before month two.
Every positive reply gets a tracked follow-up path, and the positives-to-booked ratio sits on the scoreboard at every review call.

expectations.greatMeeting: An owner-operated practice, the decision-maker actually on the call, profitable enough to afford you.

openQuestions.q: What does an everyday retainer client pay you per month?
openQuestions.why: Sets who we target, and makes the ROI math yours instead of mine.

openQuestions.q: What's the #1 problem a client has right before they hire you? What made them finally pick up the phone?
openQuestions.why: That's the first line of every email we write.

openQuestions.q: Can we use 'CPA' or 'EA' in the copy? What credentials do you want us to lead with?
openQuestions.why: So the copy claims exactly what's true and nothing more.

openQuestions.q: Which page should our sending domains point to?
openQuestions.why: They go live with warm-up this week, so they need a destination that converts.

openQuestions.q: Dental, law firms, physicians - which do we start with? And do you have clients in any of them today?
openQuestions.why: You named all three. Your call which one we aim at first.

openQuestions.q: What proof can we use? Client stories, results, reviews - anything you'd stand behind in writing.
openQuestions.why: A cold email with no proof is just a claim.

openQuestions.q: Any compliance limits or personal limits you want to add for cold outreach? Anything we must say, or must never say?
openQuestions.why: So we never write something that puts you at risk.
